mathematics.assertion_tested: On the stated deterministic grids, normalized SU2 Haar quadrature, Bessel/hypergeometric closed forms and fixed-topology sums agree for the leading two-degenerate-flavor QCD chiral zero-mode integral. Independent mass/theta derivatives, topology variance, posterior condensate, finite-volume Ward relation and canonical constant-mode measure matching are checked. The apparent Haar saddle 3/(2V) stress cancels against its canonical measure Jacobian.
mathematics.coefficient_domain: Real positive scaling mass mu=m Sigma V, real theta modulo2pi; SU2 normalized Haar. Exact identities derived analytically, finite checks in mpmath arbitrary precision.
mathematics.conventions: Nc>=3, two fundamental degenerate flavors, pure QCD without QED; leading chiral action and epsilon-regime only. Per-flavor condensate magnitude C=(1/(2V))d_m logZ. chi=-(1/V)d_theta^2 logZ. Group integral Ztilde=2I1(2mu cos(theta/2))/(2mu cos(theta/2)); full Z=N(V)Ztilde. No absolute gravitational N(V) is set to1. Constant mode has positive eigenvalue Mpi^2 at positive mass, q0=F sqrt(V)phi.
inputs: inputs.json: 5 scaling masses times6theta values (30 cases) per precision; topology cutoff|nu|<=80, 3 selected fixed sectors, 4 asymptotic saddle points.
All inputs are theoretical scaling values; no fit or observational calibration.
non_claims: The finite computation does not prove all-parameter identities; Haar/Bessel/Fourier derivations provide the analytic reduction.
The large-mu zero-mode saddle is not a fixed-positive-mass H->0 QCD calculation.
N(V) contains matching and nonzero-mode/gravitational contributions beyond the fixed local Jacobian; no c_H or c_H/Cp^3 is predicted.
Canonical constant-mode matching must not be added again to a full S4 determinant that already includes that mode.
The source's flat-torus result is not an exact theorem about all curved-space QCD modes.
No electromagnetic derivative or matched physical alpha root is computed.
Arbitrary-precision checks and analytic topology tails do not certify all rounding error.
